org.name: Department of Health and Social Care

hazard: Unavailability of Isoprenaline for resuscitation of heart transplanted patients
theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: Paul Ashton
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: During the inquest evidence was heard that The Salford Royal Hospital did not have a protocol or a guideline on the perioperative management of heart transplanted patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery
concerns.hazard: absence of protocols and guidelines for heart transplanted patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery

concerns.quote: Isoprenaline is not available in the United Kingdom and the source of the supply and the importance of the use of Isoprenaline in the resuscitation of heart transplanted patients should be brought to the attention of all hospitals and health professionals in the United Kingdom.
concerns.hazard: unavailability of Isoprenaline for resuscitation of heart transplanted patients

reports.title: Mary Fenton
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Although Tameside Hospital holds itself out as performing pacemaker insertions, both temporary and permanent, no Cardiology Consultant is on call after 5.00pm or at week-ends. There is therefore no-one available to the junior staff having the requisite levels of skill and expertise to advise
concerns.hazard: lack of cardiology consultant coverage after hours

concerns.quote: After 5.00pm there is no facility for an echocardiogram to be performed at the hospital
concerns.hazard: absence of echocardiogram facility after hours

concerns.quote: This patient was being kept alive by the use of Isoprenaline. It transpires that there were severe shortages of this drug in the hospital but also nationally. | was told that this drug is produced as an unlicensed drug by NHS Pharmaceutical Productions. If so why do they not ensure sufficient supply?
There was a failure of the medical staff to assess and/or document the mental "capacity" of the patient
There was a failure of the medical staff to obtain "consent" to treatment or to document why such consent was unavailable and why they were "self-
concerns.hazard: failure to obtain or document consent

concerns.quote: Despite this being a major District General Hospital providing cardiology cover for a large proportion of the population of Greater Manchester, there is no-one with the skill or qualification to fit "temporary/permanent" pacing wires
concerns.hazard: absence of qualified staff to fit pacing wires

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the unavailability or severe shortage of Isoprenaline needed for resuscitating heart‑transplant patients. They differ in focus: the earlier report stresses the lack of national availability and need for awareness, while the later report points to hospital‑level shortages and questions production responsibility.
links.earlier_quote: Isoprenaline is not available in the United Kingdom and the source of the supply and the importance of the use of Isoprenaline in the resuscitation of heart transplanted patients should be brought to the attention of all hospitals and health professionals in the United Kingdom.
links.later_quote: This patient was being kept alive by the use of Isoprenaline. It transpires that there were severe shortages of this drug in the hospital but also nationally.
